text:
zoe: Flagging a customer ticket: they did a mid-stream truncation (client asked to clip earlier tokens) and then resumed; ended up with two ledger rows for one logical tool invocation. dropping minimal logs below. :confused:

liam: Interesting. Is this the truncation that rewrites seq numbers or the client-side trim that only affects presentation?

zoe: Router is rewriting sequences. logs:
```
[router] 2027-01-05T18:21:00Z session=ch-900 event=client-trim to_seq=88 from_seq=102
[runner] 2027-01-05T18:21:00Z run=run-900 tool=call-exec out_tokens=12 provisional=true
[billing] 2027-01-05T18:21:01Z ledger_id=lg-900 amount=12 provisional=true key=run-900
[router] 2027-01-05T18:21:02Z event=resume new_run=run-901 seq=88
[billing] 2027-01-05T18:21:03Z ledger_id=lg-901 amount=12 provisional=false key=run-901
```

nina: So same logical call but different run keys; provisional created at first serve, then a confirmed row inserted on resume. Essentially a duplicate charge.

omar: Why is the confirmed step not promoting the provisional row? The promotion path expects identical idempotency_key at serve and confirmation time. Because truncation rewrites runtime ids we lose that binding.

liam: Two ideas: 1) Router synthesizes a higher-level call_id that survives truncation/resume and flows to billing OR 2) Billing uses a payload_signature + session + time-window heuristic to promote when run keys differ but signature matches. Both have pros/cons.

zoe: Ops/console request: show suspected-duplicates grouped in the session trace and expose an "investigate" button which links ledger rows to streaming traces. CS can then reconcile customer charges faster.

nina: Implementation sketch for (1): router emits stable_call_id = sha256(session + initial_request_id + client_resume_hint) at the very first invocation and includes it on every downstream call event. Billing uses (stable_call_id, tool_sig) as the canonical idempotency pair.

omar: Migration pain: ledger currently uses run_key as primary dedupe key. We can't change uniqueness constraints without backfilling. Suggest FF + backfill + uniqueness enforcement only after backfill completes. Backfill should map recent provisionals by matching session+payload_sig -> stable_call_id when possible.

liam: For (2), add a reconciler job that periodically scans provisional rows older than T and looks for matching confirmed rows with similar payload_sig within window W. Mark duplicates and annotate ledger rows with reconciliation.status. But this feels late-binding. Would rather prevent duplicate inserts.

zoe: Short-term mitigation: when we detect a truncation/resume within 10s and payload_sig equal, set provisional rows to "tentative" and delay finalization for a short TTL, emitting alert. That avoids creating a separate confirmed row immediately. But we need to avoid increasing provisional duration too much.

infra-bot: infra-tasks: create infra/2001 backfill job for stable_call_id, featureflag resume-idemp-ff, add reconciliation job infra/2002.

nina: Telemetry: add metric billing.reconcile.suspected_duplicates and tagging resume.type={client_trim,server_trunc} and payload.sig_hash. Also event stream: invoice.ui_event={provisional,confirmed,merged}. Console can read this to show human-friendly states.

omar: Edgecases: client retries with new nonce but identical payload; if we dedupe on stable_call_id we need to make sure clients can opt-in to sending a client_resume_hint to maintain stability. Otherwise server-inferred hints must be conservative to avoid undercharging.

liam: Operational guard: rollout behind FF with a canary mode that only groups duplicates for internal reporting (no billing changes) for first 48h. Track false positive/negative rates in that window.

zoe: I'll file eng-platform#4301 with the customer logs and suggested stable_call_id plan. Nina take console mockups; Omar/Infra coordinate backfill plan.

infra-bot: created infra/2001, infra/2002, featureflag/resume-idemp-ff.

zoe: follow-up: will post a minimal repro client that triggers a remove-and-resume flow tomorrow. Thanks. :handshake:
